title: Parmesan Green Bean Fries (F*ck or Suck Test)
summary: Green beans tossed in beaten egg, grated parmesan and garlic powder, then oven-baked into crunchy 'fries' with no potato, no frying and no breadcrumbs. Matt West tests the recipe (credited to @abandon.your.bad.habits) in his F*ck or Suck format and approves it, with the caveat that they do not taste like french fries. The description carries the measured recipe; the narration drifts on units, temperature and protein — all preserved, not reconciled.
serves: 1 large batch (as stated; serving count not given)

ingredients.note: UNIT DRIFT: the narration says 'a pound of green beans' (~454g); the description says 450g. Both recorded; the written 450g is the spec.
Narration says 'a jar of grated parmesan' with no quantity; the description's 3 tbsp (15g) is the spec.
Named in the narration without a quantity.
Description says 'Salt & Pepper, to taste' — no quantity given.
Description says 'Salt & Pepper, to taste' — no quantity given.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper. TEMPERATURE CONFLICT: the narration says 'bake them at 400°' with no unit (400°F ≈ 204°C is plausible but NOT certified by any surface); the description's explicit 200°C is the written spec. Oven mode (fan/conventional) is unstated.
Add the trimmed green beans to a bowl and toss with the beaten egg until evenly coated.

Add the Parmesan, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Toss again until well coated. The narration describes shaking the beans 'in a jar' of parmesan and garlic powder — a jar-shake variant of the same coating step; the written method says bowl-toss.
Spread the beans in a single layer on the baking tray, leaving a little space between them.
Bake for 15–20 minutes, or until the beans are tender and the coating is golden and crispy. Serve warm. The bake time is description-only; the narration gives no time.

nutrition.note: Creator-reported, approximate, not independently calculated. Description: ~285 kcal | P 23g | C 35g | F 9g | Fibre 15g. PROTEIN CONFLICT: the narration AND the on-screen cards say '285 calories with over 20 g of protein', and the spoken breakdown (beans ~9g + egg ~6g + parmesan ~6g) sums to ~21g — not the description's 23g. Both readings retained; none chosen. Calories agree across all three surfaces (description, narration, on-screen card).

notes: RECIPE CREDIT: the description credits @abandon.your.bad.habits. That handle is an INSTAGRAM account (Tavon; 362K followers / 33 posts per a logged-out profile snapshot 2026-11-16) — all YouTube handle variants 404. The original recipe was not independently audited; the opening picture-in-picture footage shows a different person preparing the beans, consistent with a credited original.

FORMAT: this is Matt West's 'F*ck or Suck' robot-recipe test — the narration calls the recipe source 'this robot' ('Let's see if this robot knows what he's talking about'), implying an AI-generated recipe, but NO AI tool is named, shown or screenshotted anywhere. AI provenance is creator framing, unverified.

VERDICT (creator claim): 'these beans 100% f*ck' — approved and '100% worthy of a save', with the explicit caveat: do not expect french-fry taste; they are a tasty way to eat greens. He claims the method generalizes to broccoli, cauliflower and carrots (untested claim).

Three cross-surface conflicts preserved: (1) beans 450g (description) vs 'a pound' (narration); (2) oven 200°C (description) vs '400°' unitless (narration); (3) protein 23g (description) vs 'over 20g' (narration + on-screen cards, breakdown ~21g).

On-screen macro cards confirmed by OCR + control-proven vision: '285 CALORIES' (~40–42s), '20G OF PROTEIN.' (~43–45s), '9G' beans (~58s), 'AROUND 6G' egg (~60.5s), '6G OF PROTEIN.' parmesan (~64.5–65s).
The protein segment doubles as a calorie-tracking PSA ('the importance of learning how to track your calories') — the macro defense is the video's middle act, not a footnote.

Capture-time metrics (1,611 views / 128 likes / 5 comments, ~5.7h after upload) are platform snapshots, not reach evidence. Channel: 42,600 subscribers. YouTube category 'Education' on a cooking Short — metadata quirk, not relied on.
Auto-caption profanity is censored by YouTube ('[ __ ]'); the title's 'F*ck or Suck' is the creator's own censoring. Preserved as-is.
